question: How does the chunker split a file into overlapping line windows?

key_facts.statement: split_into_windows in src/copilot/chunking/windows.py splits lines into windows of at most `size` lines with consecutive windows overlapping by `overlap` lines.

question: Why is cosine similarity the same as the inner product in this project?

key_facts.statement: Cosine similarity is a.b / (|a||b|) while IndexFlatIP computes the plain inner product a.b.
When both vectors have length 1 the denominator is 1, so cosine similarity equals the inner product.
The embedding layer L2-normalises every vector (in finalize_vectors), so the index needs no extra normalisation step.
The index build refuses vectors whose norm deviates from 1 by more than 1e-3, because inner product on un-normalised vectors is not cosine.

question: How does the project avoid leaving a half-written index on disk?

key_facts.statement: All files are written into a hidden sibling staging directory (.staging-<id>-<random>), with the manifest written last.
Each file is flushed and fsynced before the swap.
A single os.replace renames the staging directory to the final <index_id> directory, which is atomic on the same filesystem.
On any error, including KeyboardInterrupt, the staging directory is removed, so the final path either does not exist or holds a complete index.
Replacing an existing index renames the old one aside, moves the new one in and then deletes the old one; if the move fails the old index is restored.

question: How does the baseline chunking algorithm choose window boundaries?

key_facts.statement: The primary boundary is a window of chunk_size_lines whole lines (default 60) with consecutive windows sharing chunk_overlap_lines lines (default 10).
A window that would exceed chunk_max_tokens (default 512 estimated tokens) is shortened to the longest run of whole lines that fits.
The next window starts overlap lines before the previous end but after the previous start, and a window is emitted only if it adds a not-yet-covered line.
A single line longer than the cap is split into fragments on token boundaries.
Whitespace-only windows are dropped and an empty file yields no chunks.

question: What is the policy for symbolic links in a repository?

key_facts.statement: Symlinks are never followed, whether files or directories, and Windows junctions are treated the same way.
A link whose target resolves outside the repository root is reported as unsafe_path; otherwise it is reported as symlink.
The root passed in may itself be a symlink; it is resolved once, and just before opening each file the resolved path is re-checked and the file is opened with O_NOFOLLOW where available.
Broken and self-referential links are reported rather than followed, and special files (FIFOs, sockets, devices) are rejected without being opened.
